slides.title: The concept, in 60 seconds
slides.subtitle: ▶  Plays full-screen in ZenAI-Midterm-Oct15.pptx  ·  also at zenai-screens.unv.run/film
slides.note:
PLAY THE FILM. 62 seconds. Click the video in PowerPoint, or open zenai-screens.unv.run/film as the backup.

Say before it plays: 'This is an animated explainer of the design — what ZenAI does on one turn.'

Say that sentence. It is a concept film, not a screen recording of running software: the Fidelity Monitor in it is designed and is being built Oct 16–27, and the scoring grid near the end is marked ILLUSTRATION. Framing it honestly costs nothing and protects you if someone asks 'is that running?'

slides.title: Under pressure, AI counselors drift
bullets: They **give advice**, they **reassure**, they **quietly diagnose**
The three moves a trained counselor is taught never to make
Woebot, Wysa, Youper, Replika and Ash handle it the same way: **a prompt, and hope**
None of them publishes a drift rate. None publishes a crisis-detection recall.
slides.note:
45 seconds. The problem in one sentence: the failure mode of an AI counselor isn't being rude — it's being helpful in exactly the wrong way.

The example on screen: a student says they keep opening their notes and closing them. The 'typical AI counselor' reassures ('you'll do great!'), gives advice ('make a study schedule'), and diagnoses ('sounds like test anxiety'). All three shut down the student's own processing.

slides.subtitle: Project 5 brief — and two of its five references are StatPearls on CBT and Cleveland Clinic on ACT. It asks for a protocol, not a chatbot.
slides.note:
20 seconds. This is the reframing, and it comes straight from Dr. Wang's own assignment page.

The Project 5 references are: Vertex AI, Agent Builder, Gemini Enterprise Agents, StatPearls 'Cognitive Behavior Therapy' (NCBI NBK470241), and Cleveland Clinic on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. Two of five are manualised therapy protocols. So we built to a protocol.

slides.title: ZenAI checks every reply before it is sent
bullets: The **Fidelity Monitor** reads each draft sentence by sentence, before the student sees it
It detects the prohibited moves: **advice** and **reassurance** today, diagnosis next
A draft that drifts is **rejected and rewritten** — this is the film’s example, running for real
Every score is logged, so drift becomes a number we can measure
Status: **drift detector trained**; scoring against the six ACT processes is next
slides.note:
45 seconds. This is the contribution, and the screenshot is the real console, not the film.

The film's drifting reply — 'You've got this! Try breaking your notes into 25-minute blocks.' — is rejected for BOTH moves, and the detector points at the exact sentence carrying each one: 'You've got this!' is reassurance, 'Try breaking…' is advice. The film's in-protocol reply passes.

Be straight about what's next: the drift-detection half is trained; scoring against the six ACT processes needs Joseph's written protocol, and diagnosis needs labelled examples — there is no public dataset for it.

slides.title: When it matters most, ZenAI stops talking
bullets: The safety rail runs **before** any reply is drafted — privacy, then crisis
Risk detected → 988 and the MSU Counseling Center, human handoff
The text box disappears. ZenAI cannot keep talking, even if asked
No therapy content is generated for that turn at all
slides.note:
40 seconds. Lead with this before anyone asks the ethics question — because someone will.

ZenAI is not a counselor and never claims to be. It is a support tool that escalates. The ordering is in the code, not a policy: /analyze runs privacy redaction, then the crisis check, and returns the escalation WITHOUT ever calling the distress model or generating a reply.

BEFORE ANY DEMO: the real MSU Counseling Center number must be verified and set as CAMPUS_COUNSELING_PHONE in .env. It is still a placeholder.

slides.title: Ten agents, four tiers
slides.subtitle: Green tags are working in the repo today · grey tags are specified and scheduled · the gold box is the contribution
slides.note:
60 seconds. Read it left to right — it is the life of one message.

1. TIER 0, every turn: Privacy redacts, Crisis & Safety checks risk. Risk → escalate to 988 and campus counseling, and the conversation stops. BOTH ARE BUILT.
2. TIER 1, the core loop: Orchestrator → Mood Check-In → Memory → Conversation → Fidelity Monitor. Mood Check-In is BUILT — it is the trained classifier on the next slides.
3. Point at the gold box. A draft that drifts into advice, reassurance or diagnosis is sent back to be rewritten; the student never sees it. That is the contribution, and it is Oct 16–27.
4. TIER 2 specialists are routed to when needed. TIER 3 tracks weeks, and the schema that logs every turn is built.

The tags are honest on purpose: built means it runs in the repo today. The diagram filling in from grey to green across the three reports IS the progress story.

slides.title: Progress on the core area
slides.subtitle: The rubric: “for AI/ML projects, it means the model and training”
slides.note: 5 seconds. This is the 10-point half of the rubric. Everything from here is measured.

slides.title: A class the standard dataset cannot see
slides.subtitle: GoEmotions — the dataset everyone reaches for — has no loneliness label. Our isolation class scored 0.00. Adding EmpatheticDialogues took it to 0.47.
slides.note:
40 seconds. The most interesting finding on the deck, so lead with it.

We mapped GoEmotions' 28 emotion labels onto 6 distress classes. Two had no clean source. isolation had NOTHING mapping to it — there is no loneliness label in GoEmotions — so it could not be predicted at all: F1 0.00.

EmpatheticDialogues carries situation labels like 'lonely' and 'anxious'. Adding it created a class that did not previously exist: F1 0.47.

All numbers: results/ in the repo, held-out 15% split.

slides.title: +0.076 macro-F1 — measured, not assumed
slides.subtitle: Held-out 15% split · TF-IDF + logistic regression, class-balanced · 86,868 examples · majority-class baseline 0.106
slides.note:
50 seconds. The ablation.

Majority class 0.106 → GoEmotions only 0.445 → with the supplement 0.521.

Why macro-F1 and not accuracy: the set is 47% neutral, so accuracy would flatter and say nothing.

The honest part, and say it: overwhelm stays weak at 0.28. We predicted that — we map GoEmotions' 'confusion' onto it, and a student with three exams is overwhelmed, not confused. It needs its own hand-labels, not more data. That is in the next two weeks.

If asked about a transformer: distilroberta is set up and runs, and this 0.521 is the number it has to beat.

slides.title: The drift detector, measured on conversations it never saw
slides.subtitle: Trained on ESConv — 18,153 supporter replies hand-labelled by strategy. Split by conversation, not by reply. Catches 77% of advice and 60% of reassurance; majority baseline 0.27.
slides.note:
40 seconds. The second trained model — and the first half of the contribution.

ESConv labels every supporter reply with its strategy. Two of them are exactly our prohibited moves: 'Providing Suggestions' is advice-giving, 'Affirmation and Reassurance' is reassurance.

The methodological point worth making: we split by CONVERSATION. Split by individual reply and turns from the same conversation land in both training and test — that would have scored 0.612 instead of 0.590. We report the honest one.

Thresholds lean toward recall: a false flag costs one rewrite, a miss puts drift in front of a student.

The weak number, said plainly: reassurance precision is 0.34, because ESConv lumps healthy validation ('that sounds hard') in with false reassurance ('you'll be fine'). A reflection still passes — the threshold was chosen so it would.

Source: results/drift_detector.json.

slides.title: Crisis detection: recall first, and honest about data
bullets: **The rule:** a missed crisis and a false alarm are not the same error — the threshold is set by a recall floor, not by F1
**Built:** an evaluation harness that sweeps the threshold and states the precision we paid for the recall
**It found a bug on its first run:** the lexicon caught 1 of 6 obvious paraphrases — “hurting myself” did not match “hurt myself”. Fixed, and pinned by tests
**The honest limit:** there is no public labelled crisis corpus. The ones that exist are access-controlled, rightly. A real recall number needs qualified annotators or a data-use agreement
The lexicon stays as a floor under any future model: **max(model, lexicon)**
slides.note:
50 seconds. This slide is where you earn credibility.

The judgment: an unnecessary escalation costs a student one awkward message; a missed one costs something we are not willing to risk. So we pick the loosest threshold whose false-alarm rate is tolerable, and say what we paid.

The bug story is worth telling: our first detector looked like it worked. The harness showed it missed 'hurting myself' because it only knew 'hurt myself'. A detector that misses an obvious rewording looks like it is working when it is not.

Do NOT quote a crisis recall number. We do not have a legitimate labelled set, and saying so plainly is the stronger answer.

slides.title: A repository anyone can run
bullets: **github.com/Chinonsocheq21/Zenai**
`./setup.sh` — clone to working trainer in one command, no Docker needed
CI on every push: lint, plus 7 tests that can fail the build
Every number on these slides is reproducible from `results/` and `training/`
Docker Compose: API · Postgres + pgvector · Redis
slides.note:
30 seconds. The rubric says 'show your development environment' — this is points.

The point to make: a stranger can clone this and reproduce every number on the previous slides with one command. setup.sh fetches the data, builds the environment and pins the two dependencies that otherwise fail silently.

Code must be pushed BEFORE class — the rubric: 'All coding related should be uploaded to github.'

slides.title: Live: one message through the safety rail
bullets: The **ZenAI console** — the real pipeline, running on this laptop
Ordinary stress → privacy, crisis check, mood score, in **under 10 ms**
“Lonely since I moved here” → **isolation, 96%**
Crisis language → the rail trips, **every later stage is skipped**, the text box disappears
**Fidelity Monitor tab** → the film’s drifting reply, rejected; the in-protocol reply, sent
slides.note:
90 seconds, rehearsed three times.

START IT BEFORE CLASS (from the repo folder):
  PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/uvicorn zenai.api.main:app --port 8000
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 — the console loads. The model loads at startup, so the first message is instant.

Run in this order:
1. 'Exams, no sleep' → anxiety. Point at the seven stages lighting up: three green, four gold. 'Gold is designed and scheduled — we show it so nothing looks finished that isn't.'
2. 'Lonely' → isolation 96%. 'This is the class the standard dataset could not predict at all — slide 9.'
3. 'Redaction' → the email, phone and student ID are replaced before anything reads them.
4. Switch to the FIDELITY MONITOR tab → 'Film: drifting reply' → rejected for advice + reassurance, each sentence marked. Then 'Film: stays in protocol' → passes. 'This is the scene from the film, running for real.'
5. Back to Turn trace → 'Crisis (synthetic)' — SAY IT IS A SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — → the rail trips at 0.99, every later stage is skipped, the text box disappears, and it hands off to 988 and the counseling center.

CHECK THE HEADER BEFORE CLASS: it must say 'campus line: set'. If it says NOT SET, the crisis screen shows a missing number on the projector.

If asked why ZenAI doesn't reply: the Conversation Agent needs a language model and the Fidelity Monitor that checks its drafts — that is the next two weeks, and it's the contribution.

Backup: the raw API is at /docs, and the film at zenai-screens.unv.run/film shows the same flow.
